label: Hand-authored synthetic retrieval fixtures; not claims about real vendors

sources.text: Monday CRM shortlist: Alder, Birch, Cedar, Dogwood and Elm for a twenty-person sales team.
Tuesday Postgres hosting decision: compare RiverDB and CloudLake. We care about connection pooling and cold starts.
The procurement budget is USD 400 per month, excluding tax. Annual commitments are not approved.
Customer transcripts must stay in the European region. Do not send personal data to a US endpoint.
Search failures do not establish that a vendor is unchanged. Report the missing evidence explicitly.
Browser disconnects detach the observer. Only an explicit cancellation stops durable work.
Store original conversations before asynchronous embeddings. Lexical retrieval must work while vectors are preparing.
Alder Team quote: USD 20 per seat per month, billed monthly, US region, excluding tax, five seats.
We need twenty sales seats and two read-only finance seats. The finance viewers must not be billed as salespeople.
Nisha owns the CRM evaluation. Kabir owns the database migration. Review both on Friday.
Keep uploaded documents for thirty days unless the user deletes them. Permanent deletion must purge derived indexes.
Measure first useful answer separately from total completion time. Exclude time waiting for quota from active inference latency.
Launch was postponed because the Windows installer failed. Fix the path handling before announcing release.
Correction policy: preserve the original utterance and append a dated correction. Never rewrite an old quotation.
Meeting notes: the hiring challenge prizes architecture, reproducibility and explaining rejected alternatives.
Voice clips need explicit recording, sixty-second limits and an editable transcript before submission.
